findings.title: 'bank' is used as a load-bearing term of art in four docstrings before any docstring defines it
locations: src/Witnesses.jl:195 — "`:fail` (a hunt's bank: every witness must fail on this tree) or `:pass` (after the fix)"
src/CLI/Seed.jl:9 — "the same `select` over the unseeded manuscript at bank is the ground truth" (Seeds module docstring)
src/CLI/Recall.jl:7 — "[`Recall.mark!`](@ref) marks the banked findings that match a planted seed" (Recall module docstring)

src/CLI/Rounds.jl:8-9 — "[`Rounds.bank`](@ref) validates the lane files, classifies dead lanes, assigns ids, marks seeds and freezes `findings.json`" (the first actual definition, Rounds module docstring)
findings.description: A cold reader following the package's own include order (which is the order src/GBGCodingTools.jl loads the modules in, and the order in which their vocabulary accumulates) meets the bare word 'bank' as an unglossed, unlinked noun in Witnesses.jl's `run` docstring (position 7 of 32 files) — 'a hunt's bank: every witness must fail on this tree' — with nothing before it in the source establishing what 'bank' means. The word reads as ordinary English (a place things are stored) and gives no hint that it names a specific, mechanical CLI verb (`gbg round bank`) that validates every lane file, classifies dead lanes, assigns ids, marks seeds and freezes `findings.json` — the one irreversible step of a round (`bank: $round is already banked ... findings.json is frozen`, src/CLI/Rounds.jl:411). The same bare, unglossed use recurs in two more module docstrings (Seeds, Recall) before the term is ever defined, in Rounds.jl's own module docstring, 18 files later in the reading order. 'bank' is not in the package's own declared terms-of-art list (src/CLI/Init.jl:128: consumer, instrument, round, lane, hat, anchor, gate, pin, managed file, ledger) nor in policy/glossary.md's term list, despite being at least as load-bearing and at least as opaque to a newcomer as 'gate' or 'ledger', both of which ARE glossed at first mention in the GBGCodingTools module docstring. This is exactly the class RULE.DOC.TERMS_DEFINED targets: a noun that silently assumes context the cold reader does not yet have.
findings.resolution_hint: Add 'bank' to the package's declared terms of art (src/CLI/Init.jl's `terms` list and policy/glossary.md), and either move its definition to the GBGCodingTools module docstring (alongside instrument/round/lane/hat/gate) or add an explicit `[`Rounds.bank`](@ref)` link at each of the three early bare uses (Witnesses.jl, Seed.jl, Recall.jl) so a cold reader hits a resolvable pointer instead of an assumed noun.

findings.title: A fourth, undisambiguated colloquial sense of 'anchor' appears after three technical senses were already carefully told apart
locations: src/CLI/Config.jl:113-119 — `resolve_anchor(root, anchor)`: the first technical sense, a `file#heading` Markdown reference

src/CLI/Preflight.jl:260-262 — `resolve_hats`: "`anchor` is whether the hat runs at full strength rather than on the economy model ... It is unrelated to the `file#heading` anchors of [`Config.resolve_anchor`](@ref)" (second sense, self-disambiguated)

src/CLI/Seed.jl:47-50 — `select`: "A class's `anchor` here is a third sense of the word: the regular expression whose match in the manuscript marks where the seed is planted" (third sense, explicitly labelled as such)
src/CLI/Audit.jl:20 — `audit_bank`: "afterwards it prints the severity re-check Workflow call (an anchor, before \"serious\" is counted at grade)" (fourth, unflagged, colloquial sense)
findings.description: 'anchor' is one of the package's own ten declared terms of art (src/CLI/Init.jl:128) and, by the time a cold reader reaches src/CLI/Audit.jl (include position 28 of 32), the source has already trained them to expect it to carry precise, mutually-exclusive technical meanings: it has introduced a first technical sense (a Markdown `file#heading` locator, Config.resolve_anchor), a second (a hat/lane's full-strength flag, Preflight.resolve_hats — which goes out of its way to say the two are unrelated), and a third (a seed class's matching regex, Seeds.select — which explicitly announces itself as 'a third sense of the word' and disclaims the other two). Having been taught by the source itself that 'anchor' is precise, disambiguated vocabulary, the reader then meets a fourth occurrence in Audit.jl's `audit_bank` docstring — 'an anchor, before \"serious\" is counted at grade' — that is neither the file-heading sense, nor the hat/lane sense, nor the seed-regex sense: it is ordinary English for 'a required step that must happen first', used here for the severity re-check Workflow call. Unlike every other sense, this one carries no disambiguating note at all, so a reader who tries (reasonably, given the pattern established three times already) to resolve it against one of the three known technical meanings gets no match and no help.
findings.resolution_hint: Either drop the word 'anchor' from this aside (e.g. 'a required step, run before "serious" is counted at grade') or add the same kind of disambiguating clause the other three senses carry ('a fourth, informal sense: ...') so the cold reader is told this is not the fourth technical meaning of the package's own term of art.

findings.title: 'act verifier' / 'state verifier' are introduced as already-known jargon in a single dense docstring with no prior binding
locations: src/CLI/Demote.jl:6-8 — "the act verifier's grade of what the fix pass DID to one finding, from the diff (the state verifier grades, blind to the diff, whether the defect is still there)"
findings.description: src/CLI/Demote.jl (include position 21 of 32) is the first file in the source's own reading order to use 'act verifier' and 'state verifier' — a foundational pair of roles that Passes.jl (positions 26+) goes on to build its whole verification model around (pass_open, grade, close all assume the reader already knows the two verifiers and what each is blind to). Demote.jl's docstring does attempt an inline gloss in the same breath it uses the terms, but the gloss is folded into one dense parenthetical alongside 'class_surfaces', 'HONORED' and 'LINE-ONLY' (three more unglossed enum-like values, with no hint of what other verdicts exist), asking a cold reader to resolve five new technical objects in three sentences with no module map that lists this pair the way the GBGCodingTools module docstring lists instrument/round/lane/hat/gate. A reader who has not yet reached Passes.jl (five files later) has to reconstruct the act/state verifier split from this one compressed aside.
findings.resolution_hint: Bind 'act verifier' and 'state verifier' once, plainly, in a module docstring a cold reader meets earlier (GBGCodingTools's own map, or Passes.jl's module docstring, which already introduces pass_open/grade/close) and have Demote.jl's docstring link to that definition instead of re-deriving it inline.
